details.description: Muse Glimmer is a 30-billion-parameter dense model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, released August 10, 2026 with open weights under the Apache 2.0 license. It pairs a causal transformer language model with a dedicated vision-transformer perception encoder for image and document understanding, and is tuned for tool calling, coding, and long-running, multi-step agentic workflows intended to run locally on a single consumer GPU. Meta trained it on data from more than 100 languages and reports it comparing favorably to Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on agentic, coding, multimodal, safety and reasoning benchmarks.
advantages: Scores 94.7% on AIME 2026, per Meta's model page.
Scores 83.5% on GPQA Diamond, per Meta's model page.
Scores 76.0% on SWE-Bench Verified, per its Hugging Face model card.
Meta reports the model runs within under 20GB of memory when quantized, aided by speculative decoding it says gives a 3.1x speedup on an RTX 5090.
Supports image and document understanding through a dedicated perception encoder, alongside tool calling for agentic workflows.
disadvantages: Meta's own safety testing found a 28.4% attack success rate on the Siren AgentDojo prompt-injection benchmark, alongside 94.2% task utility.
Meta states performance may degrade on less-represented languages despite training on data from more than 100 languages.
use_cases: Always-on local coding and agent assistants that keep persistent state across restarts
Long-running, multi-step agentic workflows requiring tool use and self-managed memory
Document and screenshot understanding for multimodal tasks
Function calling and LLM-as-a-judge style evaluation workflows

sources.title: Introducing Muse Glimmer: An Open Agentic Model That Runs on a Single GPU

notes: Meta states data training covered 'more than 100 languages' (count only, no list given), matching the instruction to omit a language list. Catalog's 131,072 max_input_tokens matches Meta's stated '131,072+ token' context window and its image+text modality. Catalog lists a 2026-09-25 deprecation date for this entry; no source I opened mentions Meta deprecating this model (it launched barely six weeks earlier), so I could not corroborate or contradict that date.
